examples: I wash my hair every morning.
nuance: 머리 means both head and hair, so context decides which one. For washing hair Koreans say 머리를 감다, not 씻다.
mistakes: Using 씻다 instead of 감다 for washing hair

examples: My eyesight is bad so I wear glasses.
nuance: 눈 also means snow with a different pitch, so listen to context. For eyesight Koreans say 눈이 좋다 or 눈이 나쁘다, not strong or weak.
mistakes: Confusing 눈 (eye) with 눈 (snow) without context

examples: My nose is stuffy because of a cold.
I blow my nose with a tissue.
nuance: For a runny or stuffy nose Koreans say 코가 막히다 or 콧물이 나다. Saying 코가 아프다 sounds like physical pain, not a cold.
mistakes: Saying 코가 아프다 to mean a runny nose

examples: My mouth hurts so I cannot eat.
I open my mouth at the dentist.
nuance: 입에 맞다 is a fixed idiom meaning food suits your taste, not literally fits your mouth. Beginners often translate it word for word.
mistakes: Translating 입에 맞다 literally as fits in mouth

examples: It is loud so I cover my ears.
nuance: For not hearing Koreans say 귀가 안 들리다 using 들리다, the passive form. Using 못 듣다 sounds like you chose not to listen.
mistakes: Using 못 듣다 instead of 안 들리다 for deafness

examples: It is cold so my hands are cold.
nuance: For washing hands Koreans use 씻다, unlike hair which uses 감다. Keep these two verbs separate from the start.
mistakes: Using 감다 instead of 씻다 for washing hands

examples: I walked a lot so my feet hurt.
I hurt my foot so I go to hospital.
My feet are a bit big.
nuance: 발 is foot and 다리 is leg, so Koreans separate them clearly. Pointing at your ankle area means 발, not 다리.

examples: I ate a lot so I am full.
nuance: 배 also means pear and boat, so context matters. For hunger and fullness Koreans always say 배가 고프다 and 배가 부르다 as set phrases.
mistakes: Saying 나는 고파요 without 배가 for hungry

examples: I stood long so my legs hurt.
I hurt my leg so I cannot walk.
nuance: 다리 also means bridge with the same spelling, so context decides. Remember 다리 is the whole leg while 발 is only the foot.
mistakes: Using 다리 when you mean only the foot

examples: My throat hurts because of a cold.
Please give me water, I am thirsty.
My throat is swollen so talking is hard.
nuance: 목 means both neck and throat, so 목이 아프다 usually means a sore throat from a cold. For thirst Koreans say 목이 마르다 as a set phrase.
mistakes: Thinking 목이 아프다 only means neck pain

examples: I caught a cold so I cannot go to school.
A cold is going around these days.
Take care not to catch a cold.
nuance: To catch a cold Koreans say 감기에 걸리다 with the particle 에, not 을. 감기 조심하세요 is a warm everyday farewell in cold weather.
mistakes: Saying 감기를 걸리다 instead of 감기에 걸리다

examples: I have a fever so I go to hospital.
The child has a high fever.
I check the fever with a thermometer.
nuance: For having a fever Koreans say 열이 나다 using 나다, which literally means it comes out. Saying 열을 가지다 is unnatural and never used.
mistakes: Saying 열을 가지다 instead of 열이 나요
